For this benchmark, retain each arm’s per-user hit indicator on identical users and fixed candidates. Use a stratified paired bootstrap: resample 200 users with replacement within each category, applying identical sampled indices to all four arms; compute category HR@10 and their equally weighted macro-average. Across, say, 10,000 replicates, report 95% confidence intervals for macro HR and paired differences. For the 2×2 loss-by-recency ablation, bootstrap prespecified loss, weighting, and interaction contrasts using the same draws. Pairing preserves within-user dependence; analogous paired recommendation analyses use bootstrap differences and multiplicity correction ([example](https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-026-02282-0)). One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points.

These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted seed-42 models, training data, four categories, and fixed negative sets, assuming users are suitable independent sampling units. They do not quantify training randomness, uncertainty across categories, or negative-candidate sampling variability. With every validation user fixed, the observed benchmark score itself is deterministic; bootstrap inference concerns a hypothetical user population. Training variability requires independent retraining across seeds, which this protocol excludes. Sampled HR also need not preserve full-catalog model rankings; retain the pinned metric but limit claims accordingly ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Repeatedly selecting the best validation arm or epoch creates selection optimism; ordinary winner-only bootstrap intervals do not remove it ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Prespecify contrasts, disclose all trials and checkpoint selection, and use simultaneous bootstrap intervals or Holm-adjusted paired tests for the declared comparison family. Bootstrap winner frequencies describe selection stability, not unbiased future performance. Independent held-out evaluation remains necessary to assess the selected model; multiplicity correction alone does not repair adaptive validation reuse.
